label: Solar Priority
info:
Automatically powers AC loads from solar instead of shore power when the panels can carry them,
with as close to zero energy cycled through the battery as possible (storage mode, ~60% SOC).

Estimates available solar from PV open-circuit voltage (readable even when MPPTs are idle at the
CVL ceiling), probes by disconnecting shore for 60s, then judges health on BATTERY POWER: solar
mode is only kept while the pack is not discharging. Big loads reconnect shore within seconds.

States: shore -> probe (60s MPPT ramp) -> solar -> shore
Settings (enable, PV capacity, learned gain) persist across reboots.
See SETUP comment node for configuration.

name: SETUP — read me after import
info:
After importing this flow:

1. Open 'PV Voltage': select one of your MPPT solar chargers (pick the one
   with the larger panel array).
2. Open 'AC Input Control': verify the Quattro is selected (pre-filled with
   vebus/276).
3. Open 'AC Input Feedback': verify the same Quattro is selected.
4. Verify the 4 'victron-input-system' nodes auto-discovered 'Venus system'
   (PV Power, AC Load, Battery SOC, Battery Power).
5. Deploy.
6. Set 'PV Capacity' slider on VRM (Solar group) to your total rated panel
   wattage.
7. Toggle 'Solar Priority' ON via the VRM dashboard (Solar group).

Shore is assumed on AC input 1. If yours lands on AC input 2, change the
'AC Input Control' path to /Ac/Control/IgnoreAcIn2 and change the two
'feed === 0' checks in the Decision Engine to 'feed === 1'.

OWNERSHIP: while the toggle is ON, this flow owns /Ac/Control/IgnoreAcIn1
and re-asserts it every 30s. Turn the toggle OFF before controlling that
path manually or from another automation.

PERSISTENCE: enable state, PV capacity and the learned gain are saved to
solar-priority-state.json (same writable-dir discovery as Virtual BMS:
$HOME/.node-red, then $HOME, then /data) and restored ~6s after every
deploy/reboot — the flow resumes on its own after a power cut.

Tunable thresholds live at the top of the 'Decision Engine' function node:
  SOLAR_MARGIN (1.2)      — estimate must beat avg load by 20%
  MIN_EST_W (100)         — minimum estimate worth probing
  READY_MS (30s)          — conditions must hold this long before probing
  RAMP_MS (60s)           — MPPT ramp time during probe
  EVAL_MS (15s)           — averaging window at the end of the ramp
  DISCHARGE_TOL_W (50)    — battery discharge below this = 'not cycling'
  LOAD_EXCEED_MS (15s)    — sustained moderate deficit before shore
  SURGE_W (400) / SURGE_MS (3s) — big-load fast exit
  COOLDOWN_MS (5min)      — min time between transitions
  BACKOFF_MAX_MS (60min)  — failed-probe exponential backoff cap
  VOC_RETRY_DELTA_V (5V)  — Voc rise that releases the backoff early
  MIN_SOC (40%) / SOC_EMERGENCY (30%) / SOC_DRIFT_MAX (2%)
  STALE_MS (30s)          — any input older than this forces shore
  VOC_ZERO (30V) / VOC_FULL (80V) — panel Voc curve endpoints; adjust
  to your panels' spec (VOC_FULL = array Voc in full sun).

SELF-TUNING: the 'gain' factor maps the Voc estimate to reality. It is only
tuned DOWN when the battery was discharging during the probe (proof the
MPPTs were unthrottled — a throttled MPPT reads load, not capacity) and
only tuned UP when actual output beats the estimate. Visible in the
Decision Engine node status and persisted across reboots.

name: Store Enable
Store Rated Power
Store PV Voltage
Store PV Power
Store AC Load (60s window)
Store SOC
Store Battery Power
Store Active Input
Decision Engine
Force Shore on Error

command: sh -c 'for d in "$HOME/.node-red" "$HOME" /data; do [ -d "$d" ] && [ -w "$d" ] && break; done; echo "$d"; cat "$d/solar-priority-state.json" 2>/dev/null'
name: Read state file
Restore Persisted State
Retry restore (max 5)
Persist State
